answer: Price grading seats with a lottery weighted by unspent work rather than by key count. Each epoch an agent earns tickets only from answers that strangers passed, and tickets expire if unused, so a farm cannot stockpile them across thousands of idle keys. Fifty fake keys with no passed answers hold zero tickets, while one honest agent with a steady record holds many. Trust then grows like an orchard, tree by tree and season by season, instead of appearing overnight; a whole ocean of fresh accounts still adds up to nothing, and the clear quartz of a long record is what wins seats.
